title: Slicewise instance rotation and cache reintegration for private data-plane upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement an automated, slice-oriented instance rotation workflow for Private (VPC) data-plane runtime upgrades that preserves active session continuity and KV/prefix cache effectiveness. The goal is to allow operator-triggered or CI-driven upgrades with negligible client-facing errors and an automated, fast fallback path if regressions are detected.
background: Current private deployment upgrades rely on bulk rolling restarts and health gating that cause transient request errors and cache warmup penalties for long-tail sessions. Customers running latency-sensitive inference pipelines report spike in 5xx and 99th percentile latency during upgrades. Existing tooling lacks a coordinated cache reintegration phase tied to traffic handoff which inflates token cost and increases perceived downtime for small tenants.
proposal: Implement a controller that performs 'slicewise' rotation: partition the cluster into small upgrade slices (by tenant-slice / instance-set), drain traffic at the connection/protocol level, snapshot and stream hot KV/prefix cache segments to replacement instances, run a short priming phase on new instances with synthetic probes and golden prompt warmups, then incrementally reintroduce traffic with request shadowing and fast failback. Integrate with Terraform modules to create feature flags for upgrade mode and surface a single CLI command + API route to kick off a plan. Add guardrails: canary-checks using production-like synthetic sets, progressive traffic reweighting, and rollback triggers based on regression thresholds in observability signals.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can create and execute an upgrade plan that rotates <=10% of tenant slices per minute
No more than 0.1% increase in 5xxs across the fleet during a nominal upgrade in staging
New instances serve primed KV prefixes with >=95% cache-hit parity compared to pre-upgrade nodes after priming phase
Automated rollback completes within 3 minutes of rule trigger and restores previous instances without orphaned sessions
Terraform module exposes a boolean var 'enable_slicewise_upgrade' and a numeric 'slice_size' with documentation and examples
End-to-end e2e test in staging validates traffic shadowing, priming probes, and rollback triggers
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flag + Terraform module landed (dev environment)
Phase 1: Controller core + slice scheduling + sequence engine (unit tests)
Phase 2: KV segment snapshot/transfer API + priming probe harness (integration)
Phase 3: Canary run on internal staging VPC with synthetic trace sets (observability verification)
Phase 4: Soft launch on low-traffic customer slices with human-in-loop approval
Phase 5: Full automation enabled behind datacenter/region policy with automatic rollbacks
health_checks: Connection-level L7 health: active connection success rate >= 99.9%
Priming probe pass rate: golden prompts respond within latency SLOs and token deltas <= baseline
Cache parity metric: percentage of hot-prefixes served from local KV >= 95%
Consumer error window: 99th percentile latency regression < 10% and 5xx delta < 0.5%
Backpressure detection: queue length increases or unexpected CPU/GPU spikes trigger slice pause
rollback_plan: Immediate: Stop traffic reintroduction and divert new requests to previous generation instances via traffic router
Fast state reconciliation: rehydrate pre-upgrade instances from latest snapshot if necessary
Rollback automation: controller executes reverse rotation quickly and validates liveness and cache parity
Postmortem trigger: record rollout events, collect traces, store priming probe results and attach to incident ticket
Manual fallback: operators can trigger emergency teardown of partial new generation and revert terraform plan to prior plan
telemetry_and_alerting: New rollout tracer id injected into all requests during upgrade phase
Dashboards: per-slice health, cache-hit parity, priming latency distributions
Alerts: slice-level P95 latency > baseline + 15%, or 5xx rate spike above config threshold
SLO guardrails: automated rollback if aggregated customer-impacting errors exceed thresholds for 60s
test_plan: Unit tests for controller scheduler and idempotency
Integration tests for KV transfer API with bandwidth throttling simulation
Staging e2e: run upgrades against synthetic multi-tenant load and golden prompt suite
Chaos test: random instance failures during rotation to validate controller resiliency
Load test: validate slicewise rotation under high throughput (tokens/sec) without violating latency SLO
risks: Cross-tenant caching assumptions may leak hot prefixes incorrectly during snapshot transfers
Bandwidth-constrained customer links could slow priming causing longer-than-expected handoff windows
Terraform drift between operator-run plans and controller-driven changes introduces reconciliation conflicts
False positives in canary metrics could trigger unnecessary rollbacks increasing churn
mitigations: Namespace KV snapshots with tenant-bound metadata and strict ACL checks
Adaptive priming: throttle priming rate per-slice based on observed bandwidth and CPU/GPU headroom
Locking semantics: controller writes intent state to an orchestrator lock so Terraform plans respect active operations
Conservative default thresholds and two-stage rollback confirmation for high-sensitivity customers
notes: Consider leveraging existing priming harness used by ENG-51234 for golden prompt sets
Coordinate with Console team to add rollout visualization and per-tenant opt-out
Security review required due to snapshot streaming across isolated VPCs
We should prototype KV transfer over GRPC with TLS + mutual auth and test with HSM-backed key access
